headline: The euro is born
text: On 1 January eleven EU countries, among them Germany, France and Italy, fixed their exchange rates irrevocably and adopted the euro, which now trades on currency markets and is used by banks and bond markets; notes and coins follow in 2002. The European Central Bank in Frankfurt sets one interest rate for all of them. Britain, Sweden and Denmark stay out, and so, of course, does Switzerland.
imageCaption: Wim Duisenberg, president of the European Central Bank, at the launch of the euro, 31 December 1998
imageCredit: Danny Gys /  European Communities, 1998 / EC - Audiovisual Service

headline: Nvidia, a maker of 3D graphics chips, goes public
text: Nvidia sold 3.5 million shares to the public on 22 January at 12 dollars, raising 42 million dollars. Founded in 1993, it designs graphics processors that draw three-dimensional images in personal computers, mainly for games, and has other companies manufacture them; its RIVA TNT chip of 1998 has made its name. Revenue for the nine months to October 1998 was 92.7 million dollars, with a small loss.
imageCaption: A graphics card with Nvidia's RIVA TNT chip, 1998

headline: Year-2000 spending lifts Microsoft's sales by 38%
text: Microsoft's revenue for the quarter to December was 4.94 billion dollars, 38% more than a year earlier. Companies and governments bought licences for Windows and Office at the end of their budget years, before freezing their computer systems ahead of the year 2000.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/0001032210-99-000191.txt (Microsoft 10-Q for the quarter to 31 December 1998, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Year 2000 problem, 2000

headline: Record 1998 for Lehman despite the autumn scare
text: Lehman Brothers reported record net income of $736 million for the year to November 1998, up 14%, or $5.19 a share, although fourth-quarter profit fell to $74 million from $185 million. 'Lehman Brothers achieved higher revenues and earnings in 1998 than in any other year in the firm's history,' said chief executive Richard Fuld.
imageCaption: 3 World Financial Center, Lehman Brothers' headquarters in Lower Manhattan

headline: Record 1998 results and a stock split
text: On 29 January Nokia reported record 1998 earnings, with sales up 51% to 79.2 billion markka, and announced a 2-for-1 stock split. The shares have more than quadrupled in a year.
imageCaption: A Nokia 5110, one of Nokia's best-selling phones of 1998

headline: Public money for Japan's big banks; interest rates at zero
text: Japan's government is putting trillions of yen of public money into its biggest banks this month to rebuild their capital, after a smaller injection in March 1998. In February the Bank of Japan began steering its overnight rate down to zero. The government injected 7.5 trillion yen, mostly as preferred shares, into 15 major banks, more than four times the 1998 injection; the Industrial Bank of Japan, which applied for about 600 billion yen, saw its shares rise 35%.
imageCaption: Masaru Hayami, governor of the Bank of Japan (left)

headline: Dow 10,000
text: The Dow Jones average closed above 10,000 for the first time on 29 March, celebrated on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange with party hats. It was below 4,000 at the start of 1995.
imageCaption: People in front of the New York Stock Exchange at lunchtime, November 1997

headline: Amazon backs Pets.com
text: Amazon led a $10.5 million investment in Pets.com, a San Francisco start-up that sells pet food and supplies online, taking a majority stake. Amazon is investing in a string of young online shops.
imageCaption: Jeff Bezos, 2026

headline: eBay raises $700 million at $170 a share
text: eBay sold 4.25 million new shares at $170 each, raising about $696 million. Its online revenue grew 74% in the first quarter over the previous quarter. Its registered users passed 2.1 million at the end of 1998, when revenue for the year reached $47 million.
imageCaption: eBay's headquarters in San Jose, California

headline: OPEC's cuts take effect and oil shares soar
text: On 23 March OPEC and other producers agreed to cut output by a combined 2.1 million barrels a day from 1 April. US crude, about 12 dollars at the end of February, closed April at 18.69 dollars. Exxon's shares jumped as investors bet that the oil glut is ending.
imageCaption: The headquarters of OPEC in Vienna

headline: Enron's profit up 18% as trading booms
text: Enron's first-quarter net income rose 18% to $253 million, or 68 cents a share, from $214 million a year earlier. Earnings from selling gas and power and managing the contracts rose 74% to $224 million, and chairman Kenneth Lay said he expects 1999 to be another excellent year for earnings and shareholder returns.
imageCaption: Houston's downtown ballpark, whose naming rights Enron bought in 1999

headline: Britain will sell half its gold
text: On 7 May the British government said it would sell about 395 tonnes of gold, roughly half its reserves, in auctions from July; gold stood at 282.40 dollars that day. Gold averaged 276 dollars in May, its lowest monthly average since 1979. With inflation around 2 percent (April) and shares booming, few investors want a metal that pays nothing.
imageCaption: Gordon Brown, Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer

headline: Wal-Mart buys Britain's Asda for 10.8 billion dollars
text: On 14 June Wal-Mart agreed to pay 6.7 billion pounds, about 10.8 billion dollars or 220 pence a share in cash, for Asda, Britain's third-largest supermarket chain. Its offer trumped a merger planned with the British retailer Kingfisher, which withdrew. Asda's board recommends the bid.
imageCaption: An Asda supermarket, Britain

headline: eBay's website goes down for nearly a day
text: eBay's website suffered a major outage on June 10, halting auctions across the site. The company is crediting users $3.9 million in fees and has started a full review of its systems.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065088/0001012870-99-002671.txt (10-Q for the quarter to June 30, 1999, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: 19-inch rack, 2006

headline: Enron floats its water business, Azurix
text: Enron sold part of its water company Azurix, built around Britain's Wessex Water, to the public in a stock market listing in June.
imageCaption: A Wessex Water water tower in England

headline: Belgian schoolchildren fall ill: Coca-Cola's biggest recall
text: Dozens of schoolchildren in Belgium became ill after drinking Coca-Cola products, and about 250 consumers in Belgium and France reported illnesses. Belgium and France temporarily banned the company's drinks and Coca-Cola recalled about 14 million cases in five European countries, the largest recall in its history. The drinks came from plants run by Coca-Cola Enterprises. Critics say the company was slow to take it seriously and apologise.
source: https://www.company-histories.com/The-CocaCola-Company-Company-History.html (read 2026-10-03; it misdates the scare to 1998); https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-sep-04-fi-6777-story.html (June date, 250 consumers, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A European Coca-Cola can

headline: Police storm Tehran University dormitories; students protest for days
text: After students protested on 8 July against the closing of the reformist newspaper Salam, police and plainclothes militiamen raided a Tehran University dormitory before dawn on 9 July, beating students and setting rooms on fire; at least one student was killed. Protests spread over the following days, with tens of thousands of students in Tehran and other cities, before they were put down and many were arrested.
imageCaption: A woman photographs and a masked student crosses an emptied Tehran street during the student protests of July 1999

headline: eBay's growth slows after the outage
text: eBay's online revenue grew only 12% in the second quarter over the first, or 27% without the outage credits, after 74% the quarter before. Total revenue was $49.5 million, against $19.5 million a year earlier.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065088/0001012870-99-002671.txt (10-Q for the quarter to June 30, 1999, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Meg Whitman, 2022

headline: Schlumberger to hand its drilling rigs to Transocean
text: On 12 July Schlumberger agreed to spin off Sedco Forex, its offshore and land drilling business, to its shareholders and merge it with the offshore driller Transocean, a 3.2 billion dollar share deal. Shareholders will receive Sedco Forex shares that become shares of the combined company, Transocean Sedco Forex.
source: Schlumberger Form 8-K of 10 January 2000 (merger agreement dated 12 July 1999; pro forma figures), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/87347/0000899243-00-000031.txt (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transocean (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Transocean No. 4 jack-up drilling rig at Eemshaven, 1990

headline: IBJ, Fuji and Dai-Ichi Kangyo to form the world's biggest bank
text: On 20 August the Industrial Bank of Japan, Fuji Bank and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank agreed to combine under a joint holding company to be formed in autumn 2000, with full reorganisation by spring 2002. The group will have more than 1.2 trillion dollars of assets, ahead of Deutsche Bank, and plans to close 150 branches and cut 6,000 jobs. The three banks' shares rose almost 12% on reports the day before.
imageCaption: The head office of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank in Hibiya, Tokyo, one of the three banks to merge with IBJ

headline: Cisco pays $7.4 billion in stock to enter optical networking
text: Cisco agreed on August 25 to buy Cerent and Monterey Networks, two young makers of optical transport equipment, for a combined $7.4 billion in Cisco shares, its largest purchase so far. Earlier in the month it agreed to invest $1.05 billion in KPMG Consulting. Sales in the quarter to April had risen 44% to $3.15 billion.
imageCaption: The ONS 15454 optical transport system, the product line Cisco was buying with Cerent
imageCredit: Cisco Systems (Center for Cisco Heritage archive, Computer History Museum)

headline: Nvidia announces the GeForce 256
text: On 31 August Nvidia announced the GeForce 256, which it calls the world's first graphics processing unit, or GPU: a single chip that also does the geometry and lighting calculations that until now were left to the computer's main processor. It is due in October.
imageCaption: A VisionTek graphics card with Nvidia's GeForce 256, 1999

headline: Coca-Cola warns: fourth quarterly profit decline in a row
text: On 3 September Coca-Cola warned that third-quarter earnings will fall short of forecasts, at 34 to 35 cents a share against 36 expected, because of weak sales abroad and higher marketing costs, and that the European recall will cut another 2 to 3 cents. It would be the fourth straight quarter of lower earnings. In June chairman Ivester had said 'the worst is behind us.' The shares lost about 19% in September.
imageCaption: Coca-Cola headquarters tower, Atlanta

headline: 147 million online, and a book called 'Dow 36,000'
text: At the start of this year 147 million people used the internet, again twice as many as the year before. The forecasts grow with it. A new book by James Glassman and Kevin Hassett, 'Dow 36,000', argues that shares are still far too cheap: the Dow Jones index of big American companies should stand about four times higher than today, at 36,000, within a few years.
source: https://www.stackscale.com/blog/internet-evolution-statistics/ (search result read 2026-10-04); https://www.allaboutmarketresearch.com/internet.htm (search result read 2026-10-04) (figures of Internet World Stats); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dow_36,000 (read 2026-10-04)
imageCaption: James K. Glassman, 2007

headline: Florida court revives a giant smokers' class action: bankruptcy fears
text: In July a Miami jury in the Engle class action found the tobacco companies liable to Florida's sick smokers, estimated at 500,000 to a million people. In October a panel of three appeals judges ruled that punitive damages must be decided in one lump sum for the whole class, and analysts say they could exceed 300 billion dollars. Philip Morris shares fell to about 21 dollars, down almost 40% since August; experts say bankruptcy of the tobacco companies is a real possibility. This year Philip Morris began saying on its website, for the first time, that smoking can cause lung cancer and other diseases.
imageCaption: Dade County Courthouse, Miami, Florida

headline: Europe's central banks agree to limit gold sales, and gold jumps
text: On 26 September fifteen European central banks agreed in Washington to sell no more than about 400 tonnes of gold a year, 2,000 tonnes over five years, and not to expand their gold lending. The price jumped: gold averaged 311 dollars in October, 17 percent above September and up from a 20-year low of 252.80 dollars on 20 July.
imageCaption: Shoppers at a goldsmith's window in Hatton Garden, London, as gold jumps after the central banks' agreement to limit sales, 28 September 1999
imageCredit: Photo by ADRIAN DENNIS/AFP via Getty Images

headline: Congress nears repeal of the wall between banks and Wall Street
text: House and Senate negotiators are working out the final version of a law that would repeal the parts of the 1933 Glass-Steagall Act separating banks, securities firms and insurers. Democrats have agreed to support it after Republicans strengthened lending rules for poor neighbourhoods and added privacy protections. For Citigroup, which was formed in 1998 on a temporary waiver, the law would make its structure permanent. Its shares rose 23% in October.
imageCaption: Phil Gramm

headline: Coca-Cola shares bounce as key markets recover
text: Coca-Cola reported on 21 October that third-quarter profit fell 11% to 787 million dollars, the fourth decline in a row, but said sales in Japan, Mexico, Brazil and the United States, four of its five biggest markets, were 'very encouraging' and that most European markets were back to their levels before the recall. It also plans to refresh the Coca-Cola Classic look and bring back the 'Enjoy' slogan in 2000. The shares, down 20% for the year before the results, gained about 22% in October.
imageCaption: Coca-Cola neon sign, Atlanta

headline: IBM pulls its PCs out of the shops
text: IBM said it will stop selling personal computers in retail stores, where its market share has fallen far behind Compaq and Dell, and will fold its PC company into its Personal Systems Group. Business sales and services go on.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_IBM (read 2026-10-03, citing NYT 1999-10-25 'The Strategy For I.B.M.: Loss-Leader PC Sales' and 1999-10-22 'Big Blue to combine PC division with PSG')
imageCaption: An IBM Aptiva home computer of the mid-1990s

headline: The GeForce sells, and Nvidia's revenue nearly triples
text: The GeForce 256 went on sale on 11 October and is in strong demand at higher prices than older chips. Nvidia's revenue for the first nine months of its financial year was 246.1 million dollars, 184% more than a year earlier, driven by its RIVA TNT2 chips and the new GeForce.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/0001012870-99-004592.txt (Nvidia 10-Q for the quarter to October 1999, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_256 (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Canopus graphics card with Nvidia's GeForce 256, 1999

headline: Nearly ten million Americans now trade shares online
text: On 22 November the SEC, America's stock market regulator, reported that online brokerage accounts have almost tripled, from 3.7 million in 1997 to 9.7 million by the middle of 1999. More than half a million trades a day are now placed over the internet, against fewer than 100,000 in 1996, and online trades made up 15.9 percent of all share trades early this year. Some of the new investors are day traders who buy shares in the morning and sell them in the afternoon, often with borrowed money, and stories of people quitting their jobs to trade are common.
source: SEC special study 'On-Line Brokerage: Keeping Apace of Cyberspace', 22 November 1999, https://www.sec.gov/news/studies/cyberspace.htm (read 2026-10-04); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day_trading (read 2026-10-04)
imageCaption: Day trading, 2026

headline: ExxonMobil is born
text: The Federal Trade Commission approved the merger on 30 November, after Exxon and Mobil agreed to sell 2,431 petrol stations and other assets, and the deal closed the same day. Shareholders had approved the 81.2 billion dollar merger in May. The new Exxon Mobil Corporation, based in Irving, Texas, is the world's largest oil company and keeps the Exxon, Mobil and Esso brands.
imageCaption: ExxonMobil's downtown Houston office building, with the company flag

headline: Yeltsin resigns; Putin takes over
text: In a televised New Year's Eve address on 31 December Boris Yeltsin resigned as president of Russia and named his prime minister, Vladimir Putin, as acting president. Putin, a former KGB officer, became prime minister only in August. A presidential election must be held within three months.
imageCaption: Boris Yeltsin and Vladimir Putin, Moscow, 31 December 1999

headline: The Nasdaq ends 1999 up 86%, above 4,000
text: The Nasdaq closed above 4,000 for the first time on 29 December, less than two months after first passing 3,000 on 3 November. It rose 22% in December alone and 85.6% in 1999, against 19.5% for the S&P 500. Telecom, phone and internet names led: Sony rose 55% in December, Nokia 36%.
imageCaption: Nasdaq, 2026

headline: VA Linux jumps 698% on its first day; a web address sells for 7.5 million dollars
text: On 9 December VA Linux, a company named after the free Linux operating system, went public at 30 dollars a share; the shares opened at 299 and closed at 239.25, up 698 percent, the biggest first-day gain on record. Web addresses have become prized too: this year Marc Ostrofsky sold the name business.com for 7.5 million dollars, a record price for a domain name; he had paid 150,000 dollars for it in the mid-1990s.
imageCaption: Linus Torvalds, 2014

headline: Ivester to retire after two and a half years
text: Coca-Cola surprised investors in December by announcing that chairman and chief executive Douglas Ivester will retire in early 2000, after only about two and a half years in charge and seven quarters of falling earnings. Douglas Daft, an Australian who has spent 30 years with the company and runs its Middle and Far East and Africa business, was named president and is to take over as chairman and chief executive. The shares lost about 13% in December.
imageCaption: One Coca-Cola Plaza, company headquarters, Atlanta
